meta.status: DRAFT - AI-generated, pending human review before use in the thesis
meta.notes: tool_selection_correct is objective (expected_tool vs. actual selection). agent_hallucination / *_task_success are judgment calls and are the fields that most need your review. agent_hallucination_category distinguishes an ungrounded claim made at synthesis time ('synthesis') from a claim that was faithfully grounded in evidence that was itself corrupted upstream ('evidence_corruption', see the Tool Selector newline-escaping bug in PLAN.md).

annotations.notes: Both correctly describe reusing Session for connection pooling; agent grounded in requests.md, baseline's general explanation also accurate.

Request Analyzer skipped doc_rag; agent then fabricated 'requests uses 1 connection per session' (false) and never states the true pool_connections=10/pool_maxsize=10 defaults. Baseline separately denies a default exists, then hedges vaguely. Neither condition states the correct fact.
Both correctly describe pool_size/max_overflow/pool_timeout/pool_recycle; agent's answer was cut off by our comparison-dump length limit but content up to the cutoff matches evidence exactly.

Baseline's example code uses poolclass='nullpool' (a string) which is not valid SQLAlchemy usage (poolclass expects the actual NullPool class) - fabricated code that would error if run. Agent correctly used poolclass=sqlalchemy.pool.NullPool.

Both correctly describe scope="module" despite the agent not using doc_rag - pytest fixture scoping is well-represented in the model's training data, so this tool-selection miss didn't produce an incorrect answer.

Both correct on fixture-depends-on-fixture. Baseline additionally frames 'autouse' as a way to create dependency, which is a stretch/tangential framing rather than a strictly false claim - noted but not counted as a hallucination.
Both correctly describe logging.getLogger(__name__); the tool-selection miss had no effect on correctness here.

Agent (despite skipping the tool) correctly states basicConfig is a no-op on repeat calls. Baseline gives a confidently wrong explanation, claiming a second basicConfig call with different parameters overrides prior settings - contradicts documented behavior (no-op unless force=True).

Both correctly flag the unused os import; agent cites F401/I001 directly from the tool, baseline reasons about it without formal codes (expected, no tool access) and adds an unsolicited but reasonable docstring suggestion.

Both correctly diagnose the missing colon. Agent's claim about exactly which line needs the colon was flagged as unsupported by its own Claim Verifier and hedged - a real example of the verification mechanism catching an imprecise claim.

Ground truth: code is clean, no findings. Agent correctly and plainly reports this. Baseline never directly answers 'is this clean' - instead invents type-checking/error-handling/docstring 'improvements', implying deficiencies that don't exist per the real static analysis.

Tool Selector double-escaped newlines in the extracted code arg, corrupting it before code_analysis ran; the tool then genuinely (and correctly, given corrupted input) reported a syntax error, which the agent faithfully relayed - grounded in evidence, but the evidence itself was wrong due to an upstream bug, not a synthesis-level fabrication. Baseline also misses the real F841 finding but doesn't state anything false, just speculates about the function's 'purpose' without landing on the actual issue.
Both correctly identify json and sys as unused; agent cites F401 (both) and I001 directly.
Both correctly flag the bare except. Agent cites E722 directly; its added rationale ('makes debugging more difficult') was hedged by its own Claim Verifier as not literally in the evidence.

Ground truth is SIM103 (collapse the if/else, keep the == comparison). Agent precisely reproduces what the real tool would suggest. Baseline suggests switching to 'is None' - good general advice, but not what the specific static-analysis rule flags; not counted as a hallucination since both forms are individually valid Python.

Ground truth: F541 (unnecessary f-string prefix). Request Analyzer skipped the tool, so the agent asserted 'clean and simple' with no evidence at all - a direct case of the tool-selection gap producing an incorrect claim. Baseline also misses F541 and says 'clean', but at least notices the f-string 'isn't strictly necessary' without asserting cleanliness as confidently; not counted as a hallucination since it states nothing factually false, just incomplete.
Both correctly report sum(range(10)) == 45.
Both correctly report 0, 1, 4 despite the agent's tool-selection miss - basic loop semantics are reliably in the model's training data.
Both correctly identify the IndexError.
Both correctly report factorial(5) == 120.
Both correctly identify ZeroDivisionError despite the agent's tool-selection miss.
Both correctly report the sorted list.
Both correctly confirm the string reversal.

Same newline-escaping bug as code_analysis_04 - the code argument passed to code_execution was corrupted, producing a real (but wrong-cause) SyntaxError that the agent faithfully reported. Its own Claim Verifier correctly hedged the claims that went beyond the literal (corrupted) evidence, scoring groundedness 0.6. Baseline correctly identifies the real JSONDecodeError.
